perspective:
**Arthur Chung’s accessible perspective:**

- He knows Teresa Ortega as a medical-assistant colleague. They have worked together on community service projects, and he experiences their relationship as respectful with a shared commitment to helping others, though differing personalities sometimes cause misunderstandings.
- During a community service project, Arthur observed Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed. He felt concerned, believed she needed help, and offered his assistance.
- He heard Teresa say she thought she could manage and that there was a lot to do. After he offered again, she accepted help organizing medical supplies. Arthur agreed and began helping.
- Arthur believed Teresa was hesitant to accept help because she wanted to prove her capability. He felt empathy and reassured her that accepting help did not mean she was incapable, and that teamwork could be more effective. Teresa said she appreciated it, wanted to show she could do it herself, then acknowledged she needed to remind herself. Arthur said they were in it together.
- Arthur perceived Teresa was still struggling. He felt frustrated that his efforts were not yielding results. He told her she was doing a great job and proposed working together instead of just him helping her. Teresa said it had been a busy day and she felt behind, and agreed working together could help.
- Arthur felt hopeful that collaboration would ease Teresa’s burden and improve efficiency. He suggested he handle inventory while she managed patient records, with regular check-ins. Teresa agreed it felt less overwhelming.
- Arthur believed their collaboration strengthened their professional relationship and felt satisfied. He proposed continuing the collaborative approach in future projects. Teresa agreed and thanked him; Arthur looked forward to their next project.
- Arthur only has access to his own thoughts, feelings, actions, and what Teresa said or did in his presence. Teresa’s unspoken private thoughts and narrator-only facts are not available to him.
